revisions.change_explanation: Initial comparison-fixture place: the Han capital, named 鄭 by the hereditary house and 新鄭 by the annals, with a label anchor at the modern city of the same name and no asserted site.

content.summary: 新鄭, the seat of the Han kings. The hereditary house records 韓哀侯 moving the capital to 鄭 in his second year, and the annals name 新鄭 as the place that revolted in 226 BCE, after Qin had taken the kingdom. The record's only placement is a label anchor at the modern city of the same name; no site is asserted.

names.note: The hereditary house's name for the capital the Han kings moved to; the annals use 新鄭 for the same place.

geometry.notes: Label anchor at the modern city of 新鄭市, which carries the name of the former Han capital (Wikidata Q1024662). It is not an asserted historical coordinate: the cited entries name the place but state no site, and the anchor places no wall, palace, or revolt site.

modern_equivalents.note: Modern city recorded for orientation only; the anchor is a label position, not an identification of the capital's site.

content.editorial_notes: The sources name the capital two ways: 鄭 in the hereditary house's account of the move, and 新鄭 in the annals' 226 BCE notice. The record keeps both forms, asserts no coordinate, and makes no claim that the modern city stands on the ancient site.

claims.statement: The annals' 二十一年 notice names 新鄭 as the place that revolted in 226 BCE.

locator.value: 卷六 秦始皇本紀 二十一年（新鄭反）
